q: In the one-shot channel coding framework, the one-shot capacity with error ε is characterized by the hypothesis testing mutual information I_h^ε(X;Y). As block length n → ∞:
opts: n⁻¹ · (one-shot capacity for Pⁿ) → I(X;Y) (Shannon capacity)
It equals the Rényi mutual information of order 2
exp: The one-shot capacity recovers the Shannon capacity in the i.i.d. limit via the law of large numbers: 1/n times the ε-achievable rate for n channel uses → I(X;Y). Second-order analysis gives the normal approximation with √n dispersion corrections.
